TITLE: Educational Attainment as a Super Determinant of Diet Quality and Dietary Inequities

We then demonstrate that educational inequities in diet quality are often much larger than they are for income. For instance, absolute gaps and gradients in Healthy Eating Index-2015 scores between the most and least educated adults were 7-11 points in Canada, whereas they were just 2-5 points in relation to household income. We provide converging evidence related to large and growing educational inequities in diet quality, health, and mortality internationally. We subsequently consider an important counterfactual-that the affordability of a healthy diet is the key determinant of dietary inequities-and empirically demonstrate that economic factors are not primary drivers of socioeconomic inequities in diet quality.
